title: Formalized completeness and arithmetic provability

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Derive formalized existential completeness and the three derivability conditions for the specified PA predicate.
abstract: An existential arithmetic formula with only bounded tests says that suitable numbers pass a finite check. Can arithmetic turn those witnesses into proofs? For each fixed formula of this kind, Peano arithmetic proves that whenever it holds, its instance with the given values written as numerals has a proof. This formalized completeness supplies a crucial step in reasoning about provability. For the fixed proof checker, the system proves that proofs combine by implication elimination, and that the existence of a proof implies the existence of a proof of that assertion. These conclusions hold inside arithmetic; a different formula agreeing with the checker on ordinary numbers cannot automatically replace it.
